# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

First optimization iteration (parent = seed, val 0.520). LEDGER/JOURNAL/RUNMAP empty.
Confirmed grading contract from adapter.py + evaluation.py (see below) before editing.

## Grading facts confirmed from source (basis for every edit)
- Final solution code block is REPLAYED unchanged on 3 workbook copies (data differs); each
  output file graded. Only copy-1 preview is visible. answer_position is FIXED across all copies.
- Comparison is on `cell.value`, TYPE-SENSITIVE: number→float rounded 2dp; text exact (no strip);
  date→Excel serial. `type(v1)!=type(v2)` ⇒ mismatch. Numeric-looking strings coerce to float.
- blank/None/"" all interchangeable; `0` is NOT blank. LibreOffice recalcs formulas before grading
  (so live formulas mostly work — I did NOT ban them; that was a prior regression trap).

## Ranked issue list (clusters by leverage, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Doesn't generalize to hidden copies (pass case 1, fail 2/3) | 38332, 39046, 51359, 3911 | logic overfits copy-1 preview: assumes a pattern/pool/position seen in copy 1 holds on copies 2/3 | KNOWLEDGE + procedure | ordered procedure (inspect all 3 copies early) + "don't assume preview generalizes" |
| 2 | Value TYPE mismatch | 50630 (datetime vs str), 450-9 (likely int vs text) | over-parses extracted text into datetime/number; grader is type-sensitive | KNOWLEDGE / output-contract | state the type contract; keep extracted text as text |
| 3 | Over-production / fabrication / over-engineering | CF_11072, 325-44, 3911 | invents extra cells/summary rows; rewrites value/formula cells on a formatting task; overshoots rows; over-engineers a correct simple answer | KNOWLEDGE / output-contract | scope-to-instruction contract + "simplest reading; don't overwrite a correct answer" |
| 4 | Verification too weak | 53367 + general | step 3 only re-prints values; never checks value-is-present + correct TYPE | structural | strengthen verification step to print+check type |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | ordered procedure + missing-knowledge | task_template.md "how this is graded" block | tells agent final code re-runs on 3 differing copies; forbids baking in copy-1 specifics; adds explicit early step to inspect all 3 copies (the exact behavior the PASSING trace 58109 used); says derive extent dynamically. General rule, no task literals. | Passing tasks already compute from data / have fixed answer_position; rule only adds robustness — no behavior change for them |
| 1 | reinforce | prompt.md bullet | one persistent line: recompute from data, never hardcode preview positions/values | additive |
| 2 | output-contract | task_template.md type paragraph | states value+type comparison; keep extracted text as text unless a computed date/number is asked; blank≠0 | Passing tasks already emit correct types (48354 str, 58109 number); no change |
| 2 | reinforce | prompt.md bullet | persistent one-liner on value+type match | additive |
| 3 | output-contract | task_template.md scope paragraph | fill only requested cells; don't fabricate labels/summaries; formatting tasks keep values/formulas; simplest reading; don't overwrite a correct answer with a more elaborate one absent a concrete error | Passing tasks solved the instruction directly; wording permits fixing real errors, so no regression |
| 4 | structural (verification) | task_template.md step 3 | re-open output, print value AND python type per cell; confirm intended value+type, catch stray None/type mismatch. Deliberately did NOT mandate data_only=True nor flag "="-strings — a freshly-written live formula reads None in-session and that would scare the agent off formulas that recalc fine at grading (known regression trap). | Passing tasks already re-print in verification; added type print is inert for correct answers |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes on those inputs)
- 38332 trace: agent flipped a reasonable [0,1,1,1] to [1,1,1,1] without inspecting copies 2/3 → "inspect ALL THREE copies early + don't assume preview pattern" would have exposed the wrong logic on copies 2/3 before finalizing. Passing 58109 already does exactly this (looped over files 1/2/3) and passes 3/3.
- 51359 / 39046 traces: pass case 1, fail 2/3 because logic keyed to copy-1 layout/pattern → "detect extent dynamically; don't assume preview holds" targets the class. General, no literals.
- 50630 trace: wrote E5/E6 as datetime; feedback "datetime where str was expected" → type-contract line "keep extracted text as text; match expected type" directs writing the raw string. Scorer confirmed type-sensitive (evaluation.py transform_value/compare_cell_value).
- 450-9 trace: digit labels written as int where reference likely stores text → same type-match rule.
- CF_11072 trace: fabricated summary cells (E5/F5/E9/F9) + rewrote formula cells to literals on a formatting task → "fill only requested cells; formatting tasks keep values/formulas unchanged" directs leaving them alone.
- 325-44 trace: emitted 9 rows vs demonstrated 5 → "simplest reading; don't overproduce" + dynamic-extent reduce overshoot (semantic combo-selection remains underdetermined; not fully solvable via prompt).
- 3911 trace: replaced a correct greedy answer with an over-engineered pooled-constraint solver → "simplest reading; don't overwrite a correct answer with a more elaborate one absent a concrete error" targets exactly this.
- 53367 trace: wrote an uncomputed formula, looped 30x → verification now prints value+type, surfacing an unintended None/type problem (kept safe: no data_only/formula-string ban, so formula-recalc tasks unharmed).

## Blast radius per edit (SAFE test)
- All edits are ADDITIVE knowledge or a stronger verification step (BOUNDED). None alters a global
  ACT/REFUSE decision. No passing task's trajectory should change: they already (a) compute from
  data, (b) emit the correct type, (c) fill only requested cells, (d) verify. Explicitly avoided the
  two known regression traps from memory: (1) no formula ban / no data_only-formula flag; (2) no
  whitespace-strip rule (GT preserves source spacing on pass-through cells).

## Process & features used
- Subagents: yes — 3 parallel read-only agents (2× Explore for cell-level & sheet-level failing
  traces, 1× general-purpose to extract the scorer/adapter grading contract from source). Synthesized
  their reports into the cluster ranking above.
- Prior iterations read: none exist (RUNMAP/LEDGER/JOURNAL empty; this is iteration 1). Used MEMORY.md
  notes on prior refuted edits (no-XML ban, boolean→literal, formula restructure, blanket strip) to
  avoid re-introducing them.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The "prefer literal values over live formulas" line — but do NOT harden it into a formula ban;
  LibreOffice recalcs formulas at grading and some tasks need them.
- Do NOT add any whitespace-stripping rule; GT preserves source spacing on pass-through cells.
- The early "inspect all three copies" step (proven by passing trace 58109).

## Deliberately skipped
- 110-2 (sheet-level, 9/39 filled): genuinely ambiguous AutoFilter-intersection semantics; the
  agent deleted rows by mis-reading the task. No general prompt rule reliably disambiguates it;
  dynamic-extent guidance may help marginally but I did not overfit a rule to it.
- 325-44 deeper combo-selection logic: underdetermined from the instruction (reference drops rows /
  truncates combos in a way not derivable). Only the overshoot is addressed.
- 53367 degenerate-loop / semantic formula fix: the prompt already says "don't repeat a failing
  approach"; restating is a known-but-broken (behavioral) non-fix, so I added only the structural
  verification-type check rather than more emphasis prose.
